title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing in streaming output
author: Aisha Khan
release_notes: Fixes streaming SSE framing that could produce partial JSON events out-of-order; improves delimiter/token event ordering and adds end-to-end tests. No user-facing API changes.
description: Fix a race and ordering bug in SSE streaming framed output that could emit partial JSON tokens and delimiters out-of-order, causing client-side JSON parsers (and OpenAI-compat clients) to see invalid partial objects. This PR updates the streaming framer and OpenAI compatibility SSE wrapper to ensure deterministic token/event ordering, adds a KV-aware flush boundary for partial JSON chunks, expands unit and e2e tests, and updates docs and migration notes. Key motivations: 1) reliability for streaming structured output (function/tool calling and partial JSON arrays), 2) compatibility with diverse client parsers that expect consistent delimiter ordering, 3) reduce customer incidents related to malformed streaming payloads.
commits_summary: 3 commits: refactor streaming framer to enforce token-to-event ordering; add deterministic delimiter emission and KV-cache-aware flush; add comprehensive tests and docs updates.
summary_of_changes: 1) runtime/streaming/framer.py: introduce Framer.state machine to guarantee delimiter tokens (e.g., '[' , ',' , ']', function call boundaries) are emitted before token events for nested partial-json outputs; add KV-cache flush hint to avoid mid-object cache evictions causing reordering. 2) redwood/openai_compat/sse.py: enforce event ordering when wrapping generator outputs for OpenAI-compatible SSE; add robust handling for partial JSON chunks and explicit 'delimiter' event type. 3) sdk/python/openai_compat/streaming.py: adjust client-side streaming iterator to accept explicit delimiter events and reconstruct partial JSON safely. 4) docs/api/streaming.md: document new guarantees and migration notes. 5) tests: add unit and e2e tests reproducing previous failure modes and asserting deterministic ordering.
review_conversation: Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Found a race where the framer could yield a token event before emitting a delimiter when two coroutines flushed the same buffer concurrently. Requested use of an explicit state machine and added test coverage.

Aisha Khan (author): Addressed race by introducing Framer.lock-protected emit path and reworking generator draining to emit delimiters synchronously. Added KV-cache flush hint to avoid out-of-order re-emission after cache eviction.
Priya Desai (reviewer): Requested backwards compatibility check with OpenAI compatibility wrapper and SDK consumer; asked to add migration docs and unit tests for streaming function calls.

Aisha Khan: Added compatibility tests in sdk/python and explicit migration notes in docs; confirmed no change in wire-level events for well-formed outputs, only stronger ordering guarantees for partial JSON paths.
Marco Alvarez (reviewer): Noted a flaky unicode chunking test in CI; suggested increasing buffer window in test and adding a retry on flaky environments.

Liam O'Connor: Approved after second CI run. Marco Alvarez: Approved. Priya Desai: Approved with comments addressed.
ci_checks_summary: lint: pass (fixed a linting issue in framer)
notes_for_release: Streaming: fixed SSE partial-JSON delimiter/token ordering that could cause malformed streaming outputs for some clients; no API changes required. Consumers using custom SSE parsers should not need changes but can rely on stricter ordering guarantees. See docs/api/streaming.md migration section for details.
testing_and_rollout: Added unit and e2e tests covering partial JSON arrays, nested function call outputs, and unicode chunking. Backported test to staging and ran canary against 50 active connections. Gradual rollout to hosted infra over 48 hours with monitoring on stream-parse-error and stream-latency metrics.
risk_and_mitigation: Low-risk change to ordering semantics that tightens guarantees; mitigation includes staged rollout, canary, and quick rollback to previous framer if a regression is observed. Added additional observability metrics on delimiter-emission and token-ordering failures to detect regressions quickly.
